## Natural history notes

A small non-biting midge characterized by a delicate mosquito-like body, long legs, narrow wings, and feathery antennae in males, though adults are difficult to identify without magnification. In Florida, it is associated with freshwater habitats such as ponds, lakes, marshes, canals, ditches, and slow-moving wetlands where the aquatic larvae develop. The larvae live in water and feed on diatoms, small crustaceans, oligochaete worms, and other insect larvae, while adults are short-lived, do not bite, and may gather in swarms or come to lights near water.
